title: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle (1927)
topicTitle: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle and concept of probability
notes: **Statement:** it is impossible to determine simultaneously and with unlimited precision both the exact position (x) and the exact momentum (p) of a sub-atomic particle such as an electron.

**Wavelength measurement intrusion paradox:** observing an electron requires hitting it with photons; a shorter-wavelength photon gives better position information but delivers a larger kick that disturbs the electron's momentum, and vice versa â€” the act of measurement inevitably perturbs the system.
**Certainty / uncertainty complementarity:** precise knowledge of position destroys knowledge of momentum; the two are complementary and cannot be measured sharply at the same time.
**Probability space concept:** because the electron cannot be pinned to a definite point, its location is described by a probability distribution rather than a fixed path.

**Bohr definite-orbit fallacy:** a precise orbit would require exactly known position and momentum simultaneously, which the uncertainty principle forbids â€” so Bohr's definite circular orbits are physically impossible.
